edges.description: Premature coronal suture fusion is part of the ALX4 subtype's calvarial phenotype. The step between loss of ALX4 and suture fusion is not modelled here, because none of the sources cited in this entry states one.
The large parietal bone defect of the ALX4 subtype. As with the craniosynostosis, the intervening calvarial ossification step is not modelled in this entry.
Callosal agenesis is reported in the ALX4 subtype. No source cited here states a developmental step between ALX4 loss and commissural formation, so none is modelled.
Hypogonadism and genital anomaly are the extracranial endocrine features of the ALX4 subtype, again without a stated intervening mechanism.
Failure of the anterior neural crest stream to populate the median frontonasal mesenchyme widens the interorbital distance.

nodes.description: ALX1, ALX3, and ALX4 encode aristaless-like homeobox transcription factors required for craniofacial development. Loss of ALX function disrupts midfacial patterning and produces subtype-specific frontonasal dysplasia phenotypes.

nodes.description: ALX4 is required outside the craniofacial skeleton as well as within it. In the ALX4-related subtype, skin from an affected individual shows a hypomorphic interfollicular epidermis with reduced suprabasal layers and impaired interfollicular differentiation, and hair follicle-like structures that are present but abnormally differentiated. This is the arm of ALX4 loss that produces alopecia, and it is distinct from the neural-crest mechanism that the ALX subtypes share.
